title: Claude Products and Models
description: Projects, research, artifacts, memory and files, Haiku vs Sonnet vs Opus, and context and usage limits.

cards.definition: Workspaces that bundle their own chat history, instructions and uploaded knowledge, so related work stays focused in one place.
A conversation held inside a project; it draws on that project's instructions and knowledge and is kept in that project's own history.
A paid-plan mode where Claude runs many linked searches across the web and your connected tools, suited to questions needing several sources.
Standalone outputs such as documents, slides, designs or small tools that open beside the chat and are saved in an Artifacts tab.
The fastest and cheapest model tier; suited to high-volume tasks where speed matters such as classification or extraction.
The model tier that pairs strong intelligence with fast speed, sitting between Haiku and Opus on cost.
A more capable tier at moderate speed and higher cost, suited to long-running knowledge work where quality matters more than speed.
Match the model to the task: a lighter, faster, cheaper one for simple high-volume work, and a more capable one only when the reasoning is demanding.
Claude's working memory for one conversation: how much it can hold at once, which varies by model and plan, with room kept for its reply.
What you hit when one conversation fills the context window; it is separate from your usage limit, and the fix is a new chat.
A cap on total use over time; on paid plans there is a five-hour session limit plus weekly limits, driven by chat length, tools, model and effort.
With code execution on, Claude summarizes earlier messages as a chat nears its limit while keeping full history, but longer chats use more of your usage.
Start a fresh conversation when a chat is getting long or you are close to your usage limit, since long chats use more of both.
A feature where Claude saves topics from your chats and reuses them later; you can view and delete individual memories under Settings > Memory.
A paid-plan feature that lets Claude look through your past conversations on request; it searches outside projects or within one project but not across projects.
Each project has its own memory; inside it Claude uses that memory plus non-project memory, and turning off "Use account memory" keeps it fully separate.
The individual paid tier that adds more usage per session than Free plus priority access in busy periods and Claude Code; it also lets you opt in to usage credits.
An individual plan for heavy daily users that comes in 5x and 20x tiers of Pro's per-session usage; organizations are pointed to Team or Enterprise instead.
A shared workspace for small organizations: at least two members and up to 150 seats; it adds central admin and billing controls and SSO.
The tier above Team for larger organizations; it adds audit logs and SCIM provisioning plus custom data retention controls.
A mobile feature that turns your speech into typed prompt text and gets a written reply; it differs from voice mode and is available on all plans.
A beta two-way spoken conversation where Claude talks back and can use connected tools; it counts toward normal usage limits and works on all plans.
Claude prepares messages, emails and calendar events from a chat but you review and send; it cannot read your messages or emails, and Team and Enterprise users lack location.
A browser extension that lets Claude read, click and navigate websites for you; it is on by default for Team and Enterprise, and Owners can turn it off.
